For fried eggs, I suggest using low heat in a wide pan. This ensures that the whites are perfectly spread and cooked while the yolk stays raw. That way, the eggs are very soft. Not dry, nor fried actually. In France, we call this 'œufs au plat' which means flat eggs, e.g. sunny side-up. You can still start with medium/high heat to brown the bottom.

The most effective way to scramble eggs is to crack them directly into the pan and then set aside the yolks with a spoon. It is also more hygienic as you do not use the shells to separate them. The result will be very soft and creamy so if you prefer a firmer taste either pair them with meat or slightly cook the yolks.

top_comments.text: Dr. Hamilton, I typically cook 4-5 different meats, seasoned different ways (because I get bored) to last me 2 weeks.
